propositions: When two .bundle objects exist for the same ref on S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable.
git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects all pushes while len(bundles) > 1 before writing anything, and rebar's fetch-retry loop cannot converge on the ambiguous ref, causing push to stall indefinitely.

Upstream's Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is unsuitable for autonomous repair: it is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts that crash on EOF) and by default discards the non-chosen head to an orphan ref, losing unique events from the append-only store.

The multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at the bundle-storage layer; rebar already solves divergent heads via lossless 2-parent git merge in sync's _do_reconverge/_union_merge, following per-target reconcile semantics with --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated-history heads.

A non-interactive auto-doctor must write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any originals, so at every crash point at least one bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely, guaranteeing the store never becomes unclonable or loses data.

Concurrent repair processes must not corrupt the remote via a repair race; the helper's per-ref lock (acquire_lock/release_lock) serializes multi-bundle detection and healing, while re-enumeration under the lock provides TOCTOU safety and lets contending processes back off when another doctor wins.
